A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same learning-to-refine framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–D are readable, and retained material can be matched across renaming, relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original theorem-proving evaluations on four benchmarks, distributional tests, error analyses and refinement case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds diagnostic-format comparisons, training-data inspection, refinement ablations and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The compiler-message insertion, cold-start synthesis, expert iteration, Markovian refinement and learned value-guided search procedures remain unchanged. Kimina-Expert and Goedel-Expert clarify existing model identities; the new ablations test alternatives without changing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Goedel-Pset-v1 training material and evaluate Lean theorem proving on MiniF2F, ProofNet, MathOlympiadBench and PutnamBench. The added analyses use existing coverage; pooling MiniF2F validation and test examples changes the evaluation split rather than the task or domain.

E2.justification: v2 substantially expands evaluated controls: appended diagnostics in Table 10, Claude-assisted refinement in Table 15, and unadapted Goedel-V2 and SFT-only Goedel under random search in Table 16. Table 4 also adds the reported AX-Base leaderboard entry. The original Table 3 comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce two-attempt evaluation of Kimina-Prover-Preview-7B on 477 pooled MiniF2F validation/test problems, comparisons after one versus two SFT epochs, and manual inspection of 200 examples from each of four training datasets. Section 5.6 adds input/output-token measurements at budgets 64 and 256. These extend the evaluation design without revising the retained benchmark protocols.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial analyses of whether diagnostic placement matters, whether training targets reuse failed proofs, how Claude-assisted refinement compares with learned refinement, and what expert iteration contributes beyond SFT. Section 5.6 additionally examines computational costs. The earlier distributional tests, error analyses and case studies remain.

E5.justification: The energy-distance permutation test, p-value estimator and significance-threshold reporting in Section 5.4 and Appendix C.1 are unchanged. The new experiments introduce no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or other uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Retained result tables have unchanged numerical values, but v2 adds substantial findings. Table 15 reports 277/280/284 solved problems for independent sampling, Claude-assisted refinement and SFT self-refinement. Table 16 newly reports 46/47/63 Putnam solutions for base/SFT/expert random search, while their ProofNet scores are 26.42/26.42/23.72%. Further additions include diagnostic-format results, training-audit counts, token measurements and AX-Base's 365 solved problems.

T1.justification: The compiler-induced equivalence classes, supervision definitions, conditional distributions, search equations and probability derivation are retained, as are Appendix C.1's mathematical definitions. The revised compression and Markovian explanations introduce no new formal assumptions, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: compiler feedback as compression, efficient refinement without accumulating full histories, and strong performance across model scales. The size-qualified PutnamBench performance claim is unchanged; the expanded conclusion elaborates existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations attributing gains primarily to reusable repair and on-policy expert iteration rather than Claude, relating training-pair reuse to localized correction, and explaining decoding savings through preserved reasoning progress. Existing limitations concerning semantic failures and noisy verifiers remain. The new efficiency interpretation overgeneralizes: Table 8 shows increased total output tokens on MiniF2F.

D1.justification: Figure 2 newly specifies Lean v4.15.0 and a pinned Mathlib snapshot. Section 5.5 clarifies how multiple error occurrences contribute to correction probabilities, and Section 5.6 reports one compilation per sampled proof and value-model latency below 0.1% of runtime. These are additional disclosures, not evidence of implementation changes.

R1.justification: v2 adds Requena et al. (2026), A Minimal Agent for Automated Theorem Proving, to related work. Appendix C.3 also explicitly distinguishes Claude-generated explanations from standard distillation. The broader research positioning remains stable; the updated Kimina Lean Server reference describes the same cited work.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes trained-model names, locally rewrites the compression discussion and conclusion, and adds named analysis subsections, acknowledgements and an impact statement. Appendix subsections are renumbered, but the overall narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The tabular presentation expands substantially through new cost, diagnostic-format, training-audit, Claude-control and training-stage tables: Tables 8, 10, 11, 15 and 16. Table 4 gains a comparator row, Figure 2 is reformatted and recaptioned, and the unchanged Figures 3–4 are relocated. Appendix B.1 removes the redundant code display without injected errors.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the new controls and training-data audit make important design choices and sources of improvement easier to assess, while token reporting improves cost transparency. The benefit is limited by overinterpretation: Table 15 does not isolate the contribution of Claude's training traces, and Section 5.6 claims lower total output across benchmarks despite MiniF2F increasing from 8,197K to 9,834K tokens. The added evidence improves the paper overall, but does not fully support its new causal and efficiency explanations.
